title: Preservation before constructible restriction
statement:
Use $A=\mathcal O_E$, $I=(\varpi)$, for a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ and the categories $\Dbc(T_{\Proet},A)$ of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], with the adic datum of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Completed pullback is [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback].

Let $\square$ be the cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] with
$X,Y,X',Y'$ noetherian of finite dimension, $f$ and $f'$ proper, and suppose
there is a positive integer $N$ annihilating $A/I$ which is invertible on
all four schemes. Assume that the geometric fibers of $f$ have dimension at
most $e\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$; put $c=2e$.

Then, for every $K\in\Dbc(X_{\Proet},A)$ whose reductions have a common
cohomological interval $[a,b]$, one has
$$
 \begin{aligned}
  Rf_*K&\in\Dbc(Y_{\Proet},A),&
  Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}Rf_*K&\in\Dbc(Y'_{\Proet},A),\\
  Lg'^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K&\in\Dbc(X'_{\Proet},A),&
  Rf'_*Lg'^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K&\in\Dbc(Y'_{\Proet},A).
 \end{aligned}
$$
The reductions of $Lg'^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K$ have cohomology supported in $[a,b]$. The reductions of $Rf_*K$, $Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}Rf_*K$, and $Rf'_*Lg'^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K$ have cohomology supported in $[a,b+c]$. Here a reduction amplitude bound means containment of cohomological support, not equality or a Tor-amplitude assertion.

note:
*Source note:* no Stacks Project entry states this preservation: the
constructibility of the four outputs is the adic constructibility of
Definition 61.29.1 ([Tag 09C1](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C1))
and Proposition 61.29.7 ([Tag
09C7](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C7)), and the amplitude bounds
are those of Lemma 59.92.2 ([Tag
095U](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/095U)) and Theorem 63.14.5 ([Tag
0GL0](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0GL0)), each stated for a single
complex on a Noetherian scheme; the closest packaged form is Lemma 61.29.2
([Tag 09C2](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C2)), which realizes one
constructible $K$ as $\Rlim K_n$ with a common interval and etale origins
but says nothing about functors. The blueprint adds the simultaneous
statement for the completed pullbacks and direct images of
$\Dbc(X_{\Proet},A)$ whose reductions share the interval $[a,b]$.

proof.text: The residue field $A/I$ has characteristic $\ell$, so $N\cdot1=0$ in $A/I$ implies $\ell\mid N$. Since $N$ is invertible on each scheme, $\ell$ is invertible there too (write $N=\ell d$ and use $dN^{-1}$ as its inverse). Thus the scheme hypotheses of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete] hold. Apply [thm-weil-pbc-amplification-proper] to obtain $\mathrm{AMP}(\square;2e)$, with the stated square, invertibility and fibre hypotheses. Its FIN and interval-preserving pullback clauses are [def-weil-pbc-finite-level-amplification]. By [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], $K$ is complete and has its canonical normalized reduction tower. Its local-model data in [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-tower] imply intrinsically constructible cohomology of each $K_n$: restrict to the common strata and covers, use the displayed local reduction isomorphism, and then the finite-lisse cohomology condition. The assumed interval is $[a,b]$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin], each $K_n$ also belongs to the finite-coefficient bounded constructible category. We will work throughout with canonical reductions, not with quotient structures supplied on a strict output by TOW. Here and in all subsequent applications, the derived-origin equivalence uses its explicitly specified global finite-stratification notion of etale constructibility. All four schemes are Noetherian, and we never replace that convention by an affine-local criterion on an arbitrary scheme.

Here is the membership argument used for each output below. Let $J\in D(T_{\Proet},A)$ be complete, with canonical reductions $J_n$ intrinsically constructible in one interval $[u,v]$. By [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], these very reductions have normalization maps $ho_{m,n}:J_m\otimes^L_{P_m}P_n\cong J_n$ inducing their strict transitions and satisfying the quotient cocycle. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-normalized-constructible-local-effectivity] to $J_ ullet$ on the Noetherian scheme $T$. It supplies common stratification, coverings, local complexes and maps $e_n$ satisfying $e_nho_{n+1,n}=\sigma_n(e_{n+1}\otimes^LP_n)$ for these canonical normalizations. Thus no comparison with TOW's supplied normalizations is required.

For compatible witnesses choose bounded constructible origins $\alpha_n:
u_T^*L_n\cong J_n$ using [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin]. For $m\geq n$, compute $L_m\otimes^L_{P_m}P_n$ on a K-flat resolution with flat terms, as supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], its inverse image resolution is K-flat; exactness in [prop-weil-pbc-site-comparison-finite-level] computes derived inverse image termwise. Inverse image takes the constant $P_n$ sheaf to the constant $P_n$ sheaf and commutes with the balanced tensor, giving the canonical coefficient-linear identification $
u_T^*(L_m\otimes^L_{P_m}P_n)\cong (
u_T^*L_m)\otimes^L_{P_m}P_n$. On representatives it sends $
u_T^{-1}(x\otimes r)$ to $
u_T^{-1}(x)\otimes r$; repeated reduction agrees by the balancing relation. This gives an isomorphism from its inverse image to $
u_T^*L_n$, namely $t_{m,n}=\alpha_n^{-1}ho_{m,n}(\alpha_m\otimes^LP_n)$, with the preceding canonical identification understood. The etale source $L_m\otimes^L_{P_m}P_n$ is bounded below: its inverse image is $J_n$, and the exact faithful sheaf inverse image of [prop-weil-pbc-site-comparison-finite-level] reflects zero cohomology (the sheaf unit is an isomorphism). Full faithfulness [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] at coefficient $P_n$ therefore gives a unique isomorphism $ eta_{m,n}:L_m\otimes^L_{P_m}P_n\cong L_n$ with image $t_{m,n}$; lift the inverse as well to verify invertibility. Its defining equation is precisely $\alpha_n
u_T^* eta_{m,n}=ho_{m,n}(\alpha_m\otimes^LP_n)$. For $k\geq m\geq n$, the images of $ eta_{m,n}( eta_{k,m}\otimes^LP_n)$ and $ eta_{k,n}$ agree: insert this equation twice, cancel $\alpha_m^{-1}\alpha_m$, and use $ho_{m,n}(ho_{k,m}\otimes^LP_n)=ho_{k,n}$. Faithfulness at $P_n$ gives their equality. The same argument gives $ eta_{n,n}=1$. All source objects in this comparison are bounded below because their inverse images are $J_n$. This constructs compatible witnesses on the canonical tower. Together with completeness and the local models, [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete] gives $J\in\Dbc(T_{\Proet},A)$.

Put $H=Rf_*K$. By [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits], $H$ is complete. Use the canonical projection isomorphism $\pi_n$ of [lemma-weil-pbc-perfect-projection-formula] only after restriction to completed coefficients; we do not need an isomorphism in the quotient derived category. Taking cohomology gives $A_Y$-linear isomorphisms from $\mathcal H^q(H_n)$ to the cohomology of the canonical finite direct image $Rf_*K_n$. Both cohomology sheaves are genuine $(P_n)_Y$-modules. By [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence], the projection identifies $A_Y/I^nA_Y$ with $(P_n)_Y$, so every such cohomology isomorphism is $(P_n)_Y$-linear. Explicitly, for a local section $r$ of $(P_n)_Y$, locally lift it to $\widetilde r$ in $A_Y$; $A_Y$-linearity gives $\mathcal H^q(\pi_n)(rx)=\mathcal H^q(\pi_n)(\widetilde r x)=\widetilde r\mathcal H^q(\pi_n)(x)=r\mathcal H^q(\pi_n)(x)$. The expression is independent of the lift because $I^n$ acts by zero; equality is local and hence holds as a sheaf equality. This is an abelian cohomology argument, not a derived lifting rule. FIN from step 1 and [prop-weil-pbc-restriction-direct-image] give $Rf_*K_n$ bounded constructible in $[a,b+c]$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin], the finite direct image has intrinsically constructible cohomology; the preceding quotient-linear cohomology isomorphisms transfer this intrinsic property and the vanishing interval to the actual $H_n$. Apply step 2 to the canonical reduction tower of $H$, obtaining $H\in\Dbc(Y_{\Proet},A)$ and the claimed bound. No normalization compatibility of $\pi_n$ is used: local models and witnesses are constructed on $H_\bullet$ itself.

Apply [lemma-weil-pbc-completed-pullback-reduction] to $(g',K)$ and $(g,H)$, the latter complete by step 3. It gives completeness of $B=Lg'^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K$ and $C=Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}H$ and isomorphisms in the indicated quotient-coefficient derived categories $B_n\cong Lg_n'^*K_n$ and $C_n\cong Lg_n^*H_n$. The interval-preserving constructible pullback clause of [def-weil-pbc-finite-level-amplification] gives these finite outputs in $[a,b]$ and $[a,b+c]$, respectively. Their canonical reductions therefore have intrinsically constructible cohomology by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin]. Apply step 2 separately to the canonical towers $B_\bullet$ and $C_\bullet$ to produce their local models and compatible witnesses and conclude both category memberships. This does not identify a TOW-supplied quotient object or normalization with either finite pullback.

Put $D=Rf'_*B$. By [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits], $D$ is complete. The projection isomorphism of [lemma-weil-pbc-perfect-projection-formula] identifies the underlying completed-coefficient complexes of $D_n$ and $Rf'_*B_n$. Taking cohomology gives $A_{Y'}$-linear isomorphisms $\phi_q:\mathcal H^q(D_n)\cong\mathcal H^q(Rf'_*B_n)$. The quotient identity $A_{Y'}/I^nA_{Y'}\cong(P_n)_{Y'}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] makes these quotient-linear: locally lift a section $r$ of $(P_n)_{Y'}$ to $\widetilde r$ of $A_{Y'}$. Then $\phi_q(rx)=\phi_q(\widetilde r x)=\widetilde r\phi_q(x)=r\phi_q(x)$. Changing the lift changes neither side since $I^n$ annihilates both cohomology sheaves; these local equalities glue. No isomorphism in the quotient derived category is claimed. FIN for $f'$ from step 1 and [prop-weil-pbc-restriction-direct-image] put the finite images $Rf'_*B_n$ in the finite bounded constructible category in $[a,b+c]$, since step 4 gave $B_n$ in $[a,b]$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin], these finite images have intrinsically constructible cohomology; the quotient-linear cohomology isomorphisms give the same intrinsic criterion and interval for the canonical $D_n$. Step 2 applied to $D_\bullet$ gives uniform local models compatible with its own canonical normalizations and compatible witnesses, hence $D\in\Dbc(Y'_{\Proet},A)$. The four memberships and intervals of steps 3-5 are exactly the corrected assertion.

Use coefficient-linear perfect projection comparisons only levelwise. No new nodes. Refreshed all five quotes and made its global-stratification convention explicit in step 1; every application retains finite coefficients and the same intervals.
